thread:
maria (eng-infra): Heads-up — Copperridge asked for a dedicated commit proposal for eu-west with a seasonal spike window. Need quick numbers for GPU-hours and safety margin.
kevin (acct mgmt): They want predictable latency for inference during European business hours. Current ask: 1200 GPU-hours/mo baseline + 30% for peak? unsure.
raj (solutions): Can we get their qps distribution? If they do 2M tokens/day, batching and KV cache change GPU-hours a lot.
kevin (acct mgmt): I pushed for a sample workload but only got "p95 latency < 180ms, cost target <$X/token".
elaine (sales): Their compliance needs force eu-west only. No cross-region fallback allowed. That constrains burst options.
maria (eng-infra): Right — eu-west capacity is tight in our pool for Q4. If we do reserved commit there we should include an overflow credit pool instead of unlimited burst.
raj (solutions): Proposal idea: commit 1200 GPU-hours + 18% safety margin (overflow credits up to 216 GPU-hours) during Nov-Dec. Overflow billed at 1.8x of committed rate, capped to preserve latency SLAs.
kevin (acct mgmt): Can you show the math quickly? I need something to send to Copperridge.
raj (solutions): Quick calc:
```
Baseline = 1200 GPU-hrs/mo
Safety = 18% -> 0.18 * 1200 = 216 GPU-hrs
Total possible = 1416 GPU-hrs
Overflow rate = committed_rate * 1.8
```
elaine (sales): They asked about burst duration — we should cap single burst to 6 hours and monthly aggregate to the safety pool (216).
maria (eng-infra): Two technical constraints: 1) eu-west has a maintenance window 3am-5am CET one week/month — reduces available hours. 2) network egress to their VPC has a 10Gb shared peer limit; concurrent large models could saturate it. Need to account for that in throughput projections.
kevin (acct mgmt): Good catch. How do we fold the maintenance window into GPU-hour calc?
raj (solutions): If maintenance knocks out ~48 hours/mo of capacity in that region for a pool, worst-case we should add it to the safety margin or exclude those hours from burst eligibility. Example: 48h * GPUs-in-pool -> convert to GPU-hours.
maria (eng-infra): If their commit maps to a 4-GPU cluster constantly: maintenance impact = 48h * 4 = 192 GPU-hours. That's big. We should either increase committed hours or reduce burst allowances during those weeks.
kevin (acct mgmt): So new numbers: baseline 1200 + maintenance 192 + some seasonal cushion. That suggests bumping commit to ~1500 or keep commit at 1200 and increase overflow. Which is preferable ops-wise?
maria (eng-infra): Ops prefers higher committed (predictable packing). Overflow adds flakier scheduling and preemption risk. For eu-west right now, recommending commit = 1500 GPU-hrs/mo, safety/overflow = 200 GPU-hrs at 1.6x.
elaine (sales): That answer is more defensible to finance too. Can we offer a sliding discount if they bump to 18 months?
kevin (acct mgmt): We'll negotiate term in the commercial thread. For tech doc, can you produce a one-pager with the commit math, overflow rules, and network/maintenance caveats? I'll attach it to the SOW.
raj (solutions): I'll draft the one-pager. Also suggest a perf test: run their top-3 prompts on a 4-GPU staging cluster for 48h during a simulated peak to confirm tokens->GPU-hour conversion.
capacity-bot: Note: eu-west capacity utilization projected at 87% for Q4. Recommended lead time for provisioning new racks: 9 weeks.
maria (eng-infra): Important — if we accept 1500 commit, we must reserve nodes 2 months ahead. Add a clause about lead time and a minimum notice for scaling bursts.
kevin (acct mgmt): OK — I'll loop in legal and finance after the one-pager. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
elaine (sales): I'll tell Copperridge we have a technical proposal and will follow up with pricing.
raj (solutions): Draft to be posted in #sales-attachments later today.
maria (eng-infra): End-to-end checklist: perf test, one-pager, clause for maintenance windows, overflow cap & rate, lead time. I'll create a short runbook for on-call to handle burst ramp events.
kevin (acct mgmt): Perfect. If anyone hits blockers provisioning eu-west nodes ping me directly.
elaine (sales): tagging @Copperridge (external) will wait until we have pricing numbers.
raj (solutions): one-pager ETA 1700 CET.
maria (eng-infra): Cool, thanks — closing thread once doc is uploaded.
